title: ERIS vs Salesforce: which one fits your company?
content_html:
ERIS vs Salesforce comes down to two different jobs. Salesforce is an AI CRM that, according to its website, connects a company's customer data, apps and AI agents on one platform for businesses of every size, and it offers a free way to get started today. ERIS by Upward Technologies (upwardtech.nl) is still in development. It is being built as one system that replaces a company's separate business tools, with an AI assistant that always runs on a local AI model, either on the company's own servers or on Upward's own servers in the Netherlands. If you need a CRM that works now, Salesforce is the better choice. If you need company data kept away from outside AI providers and can wait for the beta in November 2026 or the release in January 2027, ERIS is worth a look.

Status of ERIS: ERIS is in development. It is not available, not live and not in beta yet. The beta starts in November 2026 with design partners and the official release is in January 2027.

What Salesforce is good at

Salesforce is a CRM a sales team can use today, and its website describes a broad platform around it. All points below are from its website, read in November 2026.

  • AI CRM. Salesforce describes itself as an AI CRM. It helps organisations connect with customers by linking the data, apps and agents that keep the business running.
  • One platform. It says it brings people, agents, apps and data together on one platform.
  • Any size, any sector. It says small and large customers in every sector use it, and that it delivers value for businesses of every size.
  • AI agents with IT controls. Agentforce gives IT security controls, monitoring and management tools for scaling AI across the organisation.
  • Agents in Slack. Salesforce agents work inside Slack, where people ask questions and agents take action.
  • Flexible buying. Agentforce can be bought with usage-based pricing or with per-user licences. Usage-based pricing means paying per action with Flex Credits, or paying per conversation. Detailed pricing comes from a Salesforce sales representative.
  • Easy start. Salesforce offers a free way to get started.

For a company whose main need is a CRM with AI agents that it can switch on now, these are real strengths.

What ERIS does differently

ERIS is not built as a CRM first. It is being built as one system for the business tools a company runs on, with AI agents that work across all modules on the company's own data. Everything below describes what ERIS is designed to do. None of it is available yet.

Wider scope than sales. Where ERIS stands today:

  • Meetings, meeting notes and the note taker, and the task manager are run internally at Upward today.
  • Several finished and tested standalone Upward products are being combined into ERIS: project management, document management, document signing, CRM, bookkeeping, tax and procurement, standards (ISO 27001 and NIS2, the EU cybersecurity rules), pipeline, quotes and outreach, and content and social media.
  • The main portal with the ERIS Assistant, team chat and email are in development.
  • Roadmap modules such as finance, HR, support and legal are not part of the beta.

Where it runs. ERIS has two deployment options:

  • On the company's own servers. With this option the data never leaves the building.
  • Hosted by Upward on its own servers in the Netherlands. This option is for smaller companies without their own hardware.

Both options always use a local AI model. No outside AI provider receives client data in either option. More on this approach is in how on-premises AI keeps enterprise data inside the firewall.

An assistant that only sees what you may see. The ERIS Assistant is designed to answer each person only from the data that person is allowed to open. A refused access is logged like every other question.

A log of every AI action. Every question and every AI action is designed to be logged: who asked, which data was used, what the assistant did and the result.

Instructions in documents are treated as content. The assistant reads instructions inside an email or document as content, never as commands to follow. This lowers the risk of prompt injection (hidden text that tries to steer an AI). It does not remove that risk.

A simple price model. ERIS is priced as one licence and one price per user. On the on-premise option the company owns the hardware the AI runs on, so the AI is not billed per action. That hardware still costs money to buy, maintain and update.

One step at a time. ERIS is designed so a company can replace its software module by module, at its own pace.

Local AI has real costs. It needs suitable hardware, usually a GPU (graphics processing unit) server. Its speed depends on that hardware. It reads and searches company documents and is not trained on them. The guide to running a local AI assistant on company documents explains what that takes.

Which one should you pick

Pick Salesforce if you need a working CRM now. It is available today and offers a free way to start. ERIS is not available until its beta and release.

Pick Salesforce if your team already works in Slack and wants AI agents there. Its website says Salesforce agents work inside Slack.

Pick Salesforce if you want to pay for AI by use. Agentforce offers per-action and per-conversation pricing as well as per-user licences.

Look at ERIS if company data may not go to outside AI providers. This suits companies that cannot or will not send data out because of GDPR (the EU data protection rules), the EU AI Act (the EU law on AI) or NIS2. Whether a deployment meets those rules depends on the use case and is assessed per deployment. No software makes a company compliant on its own. Whatever you choose, check the vendor's terms on how customer data is handled.

Look at ERIS if you want sales, documents, bookkeeping and tasks in one system and can wait. ERIS is built to replace a stack of separate tools rather than only the CRM. ERIS keeps adding modules after the release, so not every module will be there at launch. If the wider choice of all-in-one systems interests you, see the overview of all-in-one business software. For a similar comparison with another large vendor, read ERIS vs Microsoft 365 Copilot.

FAQ

Do I need my own IT team to run ERIS?

Not necessarily. ERIS is built to run on the company's own hardware with a local AI model, or hosted by Upward on its own servers in the Netherlands. A company without its own IT team can choose the hosted option. Running ERIS on your own premises costs hardware, maintenance and updates. Upward Technologies also offers hosting and support.

What hardware does ERIS need?

Local AI needs suitable hardware, usually a GPU server. Its speed depends on that hardware, and existing servers are not always enough. A company that does not want to run its own hardware can use the hosted option on Upward's own servers in the Netherlands.

Can ERIS connect to the software we already use?

Custom modules, agents and knowledge bases are built for a company as projects and billed separately. Upward Technologies also builds ERP and CRM integrations. Whether a specific connection is possible, for example to Salesforce, is a question to ask Upward Technologies directly.

How many employees does ERIS suit?

ERIS is made for whole companies, from small teams to large organisations. It is built to run for the whole company, not for one person on a single computer. Access is set per person. The ERIS Assistant is designed to answer each person only from the data that person is allowed to open.
